scope: Matched binary versus competing phrase-class output; development validation only.
hypothesis: Giving near-word logits a direct role in target probability can improve discrimination where a discarded auxiliary head did not.
pair_sampling: Eight pairs replace eight positive and eight TTS negative slots in each 128-row training batch in both arms. Same engine, corpus, fixed voice/preset, delivery metadata and rendering variant; exclude voice-description-only Qwen and multi-voice Piper. Independent seed 381 and same within-band phase draw; original representative inputs remain unchanged.
advance: Require matched source schedules, first 16 training batches, representative inputs and validation exposure. Treatment must have zero continuous development events and <=1% worst engine/corpus and engine false fraction, with >=3 recall points over binary control. Use control best recall within the same strict gate, otherwise within a 2% false fraction, otherwise the zero-event control point with minimum worst-group false fraction (ties: highest recall, then lowest threshold). No final scoring or board change without promotion.
limits: Existing synthetic development recordings; class labels for near words apply only to the complete paired windows. Random negative views remain other/background. Adds SOFTMAX and a fixed target projection; MCU numerical/resource compatibility is unproven.
objective: Identical source windows, source labels, same-voice pairs, weighted batches and initialization. Binary arm uses weighted BCE. Competing arm predicts other, Hey Nyx, Hey Mix, Hey Next, Hey Nick with weighted cross entropy. It exports only p(Hey Nyx). Non-target biases initially sum to exp=1, exactly preserving the binary target probability.
